headline: Van Veen provisionally ahead of Humphries as Aspinall climbs to eighth
standfirst: The Grand Slam group stage has reshuffled the PDC Order of Merit, with Gian van Veen provisionally second and Nathan Aspinall up three places.
body: The end of the Grand Slam of Darts group stage has already changed the PDC Order of Merit, with Gian van Veen provisionally moving above Luke Humphries into second place, according to Dartsnews.
Only 16 of the 48 starters remain in Wolverhampton, and the rankings will keep moving as prize money from the knockout rounds is added. Humphries can regain second spot if he wins the title.

The top four are otherwise largely settled. Unless Gerwyn Price loses in the last 16 and James Wade goes on to lift the trophy, the same four players will stay in the top four, although their order could still change depending on results.

Van Veen still has as many as three matches to play and the chance to strengthen his position further. His provisional second place continues a rise that has taken the Dutchman into the company of the established names at the head of the rankings.

The biggest mover in the top ten is Nathan Aspinall, who has climbed three places to eighth. He did not play the tournament two years ago, so he had no prize money to defend, and he has since come through his group unbeaten. A deep run, or the title, could move him closer to the top five.
Wessel Nijman also features, replacing Josh Rock in the top ten on his debut there, as Dartsnews reported. The last-16 ties begin on Thursday, and every further round will feed into the rankings.
